blocks.content: Volcanism is the process through which molten rock, gases, and pyroclastic debris are transferred from the Earth's interior to its surface.

rows: Andesitic to Rhyolitic (High Silica, High Viscosity)
Pacific Ring of Fire (Andes, Aleutian Islands)

items: Divergent boundaries produce quiet, effusive basaltic volcanism, whereas subduction (convergent) zones lead to highly explosive andesitic/rhyolitic eruptions.
The Pacific 'Ring of Fire' contains the vast majority of terrestrial volcanoes due to extensive subduction zones.
Deccan Traps in India were formed by flood basalt volcanism associated with the movement of the Indian plate over the Reunion hotspot.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Volcanism is driven by the movement of magma towards the Earth's surface due to high internal temperatures and pressure differentials.
Decompression melting occurs along divergent plate boundaries where reduced pressure lowers the melting point of mantle rocks.
Flux melting occurs at convergent subduction zones where water and gases lower the melting temperature of mantle materials.
Hotspot volcanism results from stationary mantle plumes originating deep near the core-mantle boundary, independent of plate margins.
Dissolved volcanic gases (primarily water vapor, CO2, and SO2) expand near the surface, powering explosive eruptions.
